mainTopic: פיגול for the מצורע's oil and for נסכים, the gifts of the כהנים learned from במדבר 18:9, and רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule that פיגול in the inner offerings needs outside thoughts about outside acts.
overview: The גמרא first shows that even רבי מאיר agrees a לוג of oil brought by itself, apart from the מצורע's אשם, cannot become פיגול. רבי ירמיה then fits the ברייתא about פיגול to רבי מאיר by removing נסכים from its list. אביי keeps the list as it is and explains that it means נסכים brought by themselves. Next, the גמרא asks for the source that the כהנים eat a חטאת העוף. It answers with לוי's ברייתא on במדבר 18:9, where each word 'כל' adds another gift for the כהנים: the מצורע's oil, the עומר and סוטה offerings, the חטאת העוף, and the אשם נזיר. The ברייתא also adds גזל הגר and teaches that these gifts fully belong to the כהן. Then a ברייתא of רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי teaches that for the inner offerings, פיגול works only when both the thought and the act are outside. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns this from a הקש to the שלמים, and רב rules that the הלכה follows this view. The amud ends as רבא begins a new statement.

steps.title: The לוג of oil brought by itself is a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the suggestion made just before by pointing to a לוג שמן that the מצורע brings on its own, separate from his offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the log of oil that is brought by itself: everyone agrees that its own placements make the rest of it permitted, and yet they do not make it פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. It points to a case where the oil's own placements permit it, yet everyone agrees it cannot become פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this passage, a distinction had been proposed for when something can become פיגול. The לוג brought alone breaks that distinction, because its own placements (מתנות) permit the leftover oil, yet no one says פיגול applies to it. So being permitted by placements is not enough to create פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid measure. Here it is the oil the מצורע brings for his purification.
By itself, brought separately from the offering
Its placements, meaning the oil that is put on the מצורע and sprinkled
They permit it, so the leftover oil may be eaten by the כהנים
They make it פיגול, meaning forbidden because of a wrong intention during the service

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'permits it' with 'can make it פיגול.' This step shows that something can be permitted by placements and still not be subject to פיגול.

phrases.english: But there is the log [that comes] by itself
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets comes from the corrected wording. He means the oil that is brought on its own, after the offerings.

phrases.english: where, according to everyone, its placements permit it,
and yet they do not make it פיגול!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks a distinction proposed just before this passage.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested principle that something permitted by its own placements can become פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: the separately brought לוג is permitted by its own placements, yet everyone agrees it is not subject to פיגול.

steps.title: רבי מאיר says the מצורע's oil can become פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר rules that one is liable for פיגול on the מצורע's oil, because the blood of the offering permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: For the log of oil of a מצורע, one is liable for eating it because of פיגול, since the blood permits it to be put on the thumb and big toe. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its proof for the challenge by quoting a ברייתא. In it, רבי מאיר rules that the מצורע's oil can become פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's reason is that the blood of the אשם is what permits the oil to be put on the מצורע. So the oil depends on the offering's blood, and that dependence is what lets it become פיגול. The next step shows that he means only oil brought together with the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת who brings offerings when he becomes pure
An offering made forbidden by the intention to eat it after its proper time
The thumb and big toe, where the blood and oil are placed on the מצורע
Permits it

phrases.english: As it is taught: the log of oil of a מצורע,
one is liable for it because of פיגול,
because the blood permits it for the thumbs and toes.
phrases.notes: This is the blood of the מצורע's אשם. Only after that blood is put on him may the oil be put on the same spots.

phrases.english: These are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source that proves the challenge in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the לוג brought by itself is not subject to פיגול even according to רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי מאיר's view on the מצורע's oil.

steps.title: רבי מאיר meant only oil brought with the offering
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים object that the oil can be brought days after the אשם, and רבי מאיר answers that he only meant oil brought together with the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי מאיר: But a person may bring his אשם now and the log anytime up to ten days from now! He said to them: I also only spoke about a log that comes with the אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. רבי מאיר makes clear that פיגול applies only when the oil comes together with the אשם, which proves the challenge from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים argued that the oil can be brought separately, so how can the blood control it? רבי מאיר agreed and limited his ruling to oil brought together with the אשם. So even רבי מאיר holds that a לוג brought by itself cannot become פיגול, exactly as step 1 claimed.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering. The מצורע brings one, and its blood is put on him.
But isn't it so? It opens an objection.
I too did not say it, except in a limited case

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי מאיר agrees that a לוג brought by itself, separately from the אשם, cannot become פיגול. He applies פיגול only when the oil comes with the אשם.

phrases.english: They said to רבי מאיר:
But a person may bring his אשם now,
and the log anytime from now until ten days later!

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי,
phrases.english: He said to them: I too did not say it,
except about a log that comes with the אשם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא and finishes the proof for step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The לוג brought by itself is not subject to פיגול according to everyone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's own limitation in the ברייתא: 'I only said it about a log that comes with the אשם.'

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: remove נסכים from the list
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה keeps the ברייתא as the view of רבי מאיר but removes נסכים from its list of items not subject to פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי ירמיה said: Really, the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, and remove נסכים from it.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier attempt failed, רבי ירמיה offers a new answer. He removes נסכים from the ברייתא's list, so that it can still follow רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that נסכים brought with an offering can become פיגול, so a list saying נסכים are not subject to פיגול seems to argue with him. רבי ירמיה fixes this by deleting נסכים from the list. The rest of the ברייתא then fits רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier approach and brings a new one.
Really, in fact. It keeps the original assumption.
Remove from here. Delete this item from the text.
Libations, together with the flour offering brought along with an animal offering

phrases.english: Rather, רבי ירמיה said:
Really, it follows רבי מאיר,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא, discussed before this passage, that lists items not subject to פיגול.

phrases.english: and remove libations from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that was refuted in steps 1-3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the text: one item is deleted from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists נסכים as not subject to פיגול, which seems to contradict רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Take נסכים out of the list. The ברייתא then follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: אביי: keep the text and read it carefully
steps.stepSummary: אביי says nothing should be deleted. The ברייתא is talking about נסכים brought by themselves, which even רבי מאיר says cannot become פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, do not remove it. The תנא taught about the log that comes with the אשם, and the same is true of נסכים that come with an offering. Then he taught about נסכים that come by themselves, and the same is true of a log that comes by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another answer that keeps the text as it is. He explains that each case in the ברייתא also teaches about a matching case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two pairs. Oil with the אשם and נסכים with an offering can become פיגול according to רבי מאיר. Oil alone and נסכים alone cannot. The ברייתא names one example from each pair, and when it lists נסכים as not subject to פיגול, it means נסכים brought alone, so it agrees with רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not remove it
And the same rule applies to the matching case
And then he taught
An animal offering

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to fit the ברייתא with רבי מאיר. רבי ירמיה deletes נסכים from the list. אביי keeps the text and explains that the ברייתא means נסכים brought by themselves, which are like the לוג brought by itself.

phrases.english: אביי said: Really, do not remove it;
and the תנא taught about the log that comes with the אשם,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא הַדִּין לִנְסָכִים הַבָּאִין עִם הַזֶּבַח,
phrases.english: and the same is true of libations that come with the offering,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תָּנָא נְסָכִים הַבָּאִין בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן –
phrases.english: and then he taught about libations that come by themselves,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא הַדִּין לְלוֹג הַבָּא לִפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: and the same is true of a log that comes by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי ירמיה's deletion and offers a reading that keeps the text as it is.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: each listed case also teaches about a matching case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נסכים in the list seemed to be נסכים brought with an offering, which contradicts רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list means נסכים brought by themselves, which even רבי מאיר says cannot become פיגול, just like the לוג brought by itself.

steps.title: New line of the משנה: the bird sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the blood of a חטאת העוף permits its meat to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A bird sin offering — its blood permits its meat to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up a question about where this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. The rule is that once the blood of a חטאת העוף is properly done, its meat may be eaten by the כהנים. The next step asks for the source in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering brought from a bird
Priests
Its meat

phrases.english: A bird sin offering —
its blood permits its meat to the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַטַּאת הָעוֹף דָּמָהּ מַתִּיר אֶת בְּשָׂרָהּ לַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood of a חטאת העוף permits its meat to be eaten by the כהנים.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the meat of a חטאת העוף goes to the כהנים, and begins the answer with a ברייתא taught by לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? As לוי taught:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where this rule comes from. It begins its answer by bringing a teaching of לוי, which is laid out in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the source in the תורה, not about the rule itself. The words 'as לוי taught' only introduce the answer. The actual teaching, built on a פסוק about the gifts given to the כהנים, is laid out in the next steps, and step 10 is the line that answers this question.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these words? A standard request for a source.
As לוי taught, introducing a ברייתא from him

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
As לוי teaches:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule quoted in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה that the meat of a חטאת העוף is given to the כהנים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer is לוי's ברייתא on במדבר 18:9, quoted in steps 8-14. Step 10 gives the line that answers this question: 'ולכל חטאתם' includes the חטאת העוף.

steps.title: Every offering of theirs includes the leper's log of oil
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'כל קרבנם' that the לוג שמן of a מצורע goes to the כהנים, even though none of it goes on the fire of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Every offering of theirs' comes to include the log of oil of a מצורע. You might have thought: the תורה wrote 'from the fire,' and this oil is not left over from the fire. So the פסוק teaches us that it still goes to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins going through the ברייתא of לוי phrase by phrase. The first phrase, 'כל קרבנם,' adds the מצורע's לוג of oil to the gifts of the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק calls these gifts things left over 'from the fire,' which sounds like only things partly burned on the מזבח. The מצורע's oil is not burned on the מזבח, so we might have left it out. The extra word 'כל' tells us it is included anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: To include; to add something the פסוק might seem to leave out
It would have entered your mind to say; the mistaken first thought
It teaches us; the פסוק comes to correct that first thought
The measure of oil a מצורע brings as part of his purification
Left over from the fire; what remains after the מזבח gets its share

phrases.english: "Every offering of theirs"
comes to include the log of oil of a leper.
It would have entered your mind to say:
the Merciful One wrote "from the fire,"
phrases.notes: These words are in the same פסוק, describing the gifts as what is left after the מזבח's part.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי לָאו מוֹתָר מִן הָאֵשׁ הוּא;
phrases.english: and this is not left over from the fire;
so it teaches us that it is included.

steps.triggerLanguage: כל קרבנם לרבות לוג שמן של מצורע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of לוי that step 7 started quoting as its answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לוג שמן of a מצורע is a gift to the כהנים, learned from 'כל קרבנם.'

steps.title: Every meal offering of theirs includes the עומר and the סוטה's offering
steps.stepSummary: 'לכל מנחתם' adds the מנחת העומר and the מנחת קנאות, even though they do not bring atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Every meal offering of theirs' comes to include the מנחת העומר and the מנחת קנאות. You might have thought: the תורה says 'they shall eat those things through which atonement was made,' and the עומר comes to permit the new grain, while the מנחת קנאות comes to clear up a sin. So the פסוק teaches us they are still eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next phrase of the פסוק and adds two מנחות to what the כהנים eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק in שמות says the כהנים eat things that bring atonement. The עומר does not atone; it makes the new grain permitted. The מנחת קנאות does not atone either; it helps find out whether the סוטה sinned. 'כל' teaches that the כהנים eat them anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן
The meal offering of jealousy, brought by a סוטה
Through which atonement was made
To clear up (find out about) a sin

phrases.english: "Every meal offering of theirs"
comes to include the omer meal offering and the meal offering of jealousy.
It would have entered your mind to say:
"And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made"
and the omer meal offering comes to permit,
phrases.notes: It permits eating the new year's grain.

phrases.english: and the meal offering of jealousy comes to clarify a sin;
so it teaches us that they are included.

steps.triggerLanguage: לכל מנחתם לרבות מנחת עומר ומנחת הקנאות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next clause of the same ברייתא, same pattern as step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת העומר and the מנחת קנאות are eaten by the כהנים, even though they do not bring atonement.

steps.title: Every sin offering of theirs includes the bird sin offering
steps.stepSummary: 'ולכל חטאתם' adds the חטאת העוף. This answers the question from step 7: its meat goes to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And every sin offering of theirs' comes to include the חטאת העוף. You might have thought it is a נבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line of the ברייתא that actually answers the question from step 7. The חטאת העוף is included in the gifts the כהנים eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird is killed by מליקה (pinching the neck), not by שחיטה. For a regular bird that would make it a נבילה, so we might think nobody may eat it. 'כל' teaches that the כהנים do eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a sin offering
An animal or bird that died without proper שחיטה; forbidden to eat
Killing a bird קרבן by pinching the back of its neck

steps.whatToRemember: The source that the כהנים eat a חטאת העוף is the word 'ולכל חטאתם' in במדבר 18:9, even though it is killed without שחיטה.

phrases.english: "And every sin offering of theirs"
comes to include the bird sin offering.
It would have entered your mind to say: it is an unslaughtered carcass.
phrases.notes: The bird is killed by pinching its neck, not by שחיטה. The text doesn't say 'it teaches us' here, but that is understood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next clause of the ברייתא, and the one that directly answers step 7's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The meat of a חטאת העוף goes to the כהנים because 'ולכל חטאתם' includes it, even though it is killed by מליקה.

steps.title: Every guilt offering of theirs includes the נזיר's and מצורע's guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: 'לכל אשמם' adds the אשם נזיר and the אשם מצורע, even though they make a person fit rather than atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Every guilt offering of theirs' comes to include the אשם נזיר and the אשם מצורע. You might have thought: they come to make the person fit. So the פסוק teaches us they are still eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the last phrase of the פסוק, adding two kinds of אשם to the gifts of the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם נזיר lets the נזיר start his נזירות again, and the אשם מצורע lets the מצורע eat קדשים. Since they make someone fit instead of atoning, we might have thought they don't fit 'they shall eat those things with which atonement was made.' 'כל' teaches that the כהנים eat them.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering of a נזיר who became טמא
The guilt offering a מצורע brings when he becomes pure
To make fit; to allow the person to do something he could not do before

steps.whatToRemember: Each 'כל' in במדבר 18:9 adds an item that seemed not to belong: oil not put on the fire, מנחות that don't atone, a bird killed without שחיטה, and אשמות that make a person fit.

phrases.english: "Every guilt offering of theirs"
comes to include the guilt offering of a nazirite and the guilt offering of a leper.
It would have entered your mind to say: they come to make fit;
phrases.notes: This thought goes back to the פסוק in step 9, which speaks of things that bring atonement.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that they are included.

steps.triggerLanguage: לכל אשמם לרבות אשם נזיר ואשם מצורע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the ברייתא, using the same 'atonement' idea from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אשם נזיר and the אשם מצורע are eaten by the כהנים, even though they come to make a person fit.

steps.title: Why include the leper's guilt offering if the verse already says it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the אשם מצורע is already openly written as belonging to the כהנים, so 'לכל אשמם' cannot be needed to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The guilt offering of a מצורע is written openly in the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the end of the ברייתא from step 11. That step said 'לכל אשמם' adds the אשם מצורע, but the תורה already says this openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק in the section about the מצורע already says his אשם is like a חטאת and belongs to the כהן. A ברייתא should not use an extra word to teach something that is already stated plainly. So something in the ברייתא's list must be wrong or must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: openly, clearly stated
it is written about it
the guilt offering brought by a person healed from צרעת

phrases.english: The guilt offering of a leper —
it is openly written about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that 'לכל אשמם' adds the אשם מצורע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A derivation is pointless for something the תורה already states openly.

steps.title: The verse really adds the נזיר's guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'לכל אשמם' teaches that the אשם נזיר is like the אשם מצורע, and also goes to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to include the guilt offering of a נזיר, making it like the guilt offering of a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes how we read the ברייתא. The extra word is only needed for the אשם נזיר, which the תורה does not say openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם מצורע is the known case written in the פסוק. The word 'לכל' stretches that rule to the אשם נזיר. Both are offerings that make a person fit again rather than atone, so they are compared to each other.

keyTerms.meaning: to include, to add another case
the guilt offering a נזיר brings when he becomes טמא

steps.whatToRemember: The אשם מצורע is learned openly from its own פסוק. The word 'לכל אשמם' is needed for the אשם נזיר.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to include the guilt offering of a nazir
like the guilt offering of a leper.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת אֲשַׁם נָזִיר כַּאֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to use 'לכל אשמם' to teach the אשם מצורע.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לכל אשמם' teaches that the אשם נזיר is eaten by the כהנים just like the אשם מצורע.

steps.title: Stolen property of a convert, and the priest's full ownership
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'אשר ישיבו' that stolen property of a גר goes to the כהנים. It learns from 'לך הוא' that these gifts fully belong to the כהן, enough to use for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Which they shall return': this is property stolen from a גר. 'It is yours': it shall be yours, even to betroth a woman with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going through the words of the פסוק. It adds one more gift for the כהנים and then explains how fully the כהן owns them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גזל הגר is the case of a person who stole from a גר who then died with no heirs. The thief pays back to the כהנים. The words 'לך הוא' show that the כהן owns these gifts completely, enough to use them for קידושין, which needs something he really owns.

keyTerms.meaning: property stolen from a convert who died with no heirs, paid back to the כהנים
to betroth (קידושין)
they shall return / pay back

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lists the gifts of the כהנים: the לוג שמן, two מנחות, the חטאת העוף, the אשם נזיר, and גזל הגר. It ends by saying these gifts fully belong to the כהן.

phrases.english: "Which they shall return" —
this is what was stolen from a convert.
"It is for you" —
it shall be yours,
even to betroth a woman with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's word-by-word derivations after the correction in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גזל הגר goes to the כהנים, and the gifts of the כהנים are fully the כהן's property, even for קידושין.

steps.title: A third view: intent about outside acts makes פיגול, about inside acts does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי says that a פיגול thought about something done outside counts, but a thought about something done inside does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אלעזר says in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי: If he had a פיגול thought about something done outside, it is פיגול. If it was about something done inside, it is not פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the gifts topic and returns to the משנה's argument about פיגול for the inner offerings, the bulls and goats that are burned. It brings a ברייתא with a third opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the תנא קמא says these offerings can become פיגול and רבי שמעון says they cannot. רבי יוסי הגלילי takes a middle path. A thought about an act in the courtyard, 'outside', can make פיגול. A thought about an act inside the היכל cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: he made the offering פיגול through a wrong-time thought
outside, meaning in the courtyard, not inside the היכל
inside the היכל, where the inner blood service is done

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'outside' does not mean outside the בית המקדש. It means the courtyard, compared to 'inside' the היכל.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Elazar says
in the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
If he made a piggul thought about something done outside —
he made it piggul.
About something done inside —
he did not make it piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה's argument about פיגול for the inner offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פיגול thought about an act done outside makes פיגול. A thought about an act done inside does not.

steps.title: First example: standing outside, thinking about the inside sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: Someone who slaughters outside and plans to sprinkle the blood inside tomorrow has not made the offering פיגול, because the thought is outside but the act is inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he stood outside and said, 'I am slaughtering in order to sprinkle its blood tomorrow,' it is not פיגול. A thought outside about an act done inside does not make פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains its rule with a first example. The slaughtering happens outside, but the thought is about the sprinkling inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sprinkling of these offerings is done inside the היכל. A thought made outside, during the slaughtering, cannot reach an act that belongs inside. So the offering stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: how so? (introduces examples)
I am hereby slaughtering
to sprinkle (the blood)
intention, thought

phrases.english: How so?
If he was standing outside and said:
"I am slaughtering
in order to sprinkle its blood tomorrow" —
he did not make it piggul,
because a thought outside
about something done inside does not make piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical example of the rule in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thought outside about an act done inside does not make פיגול.

steps.title: Second example: standing inside, thinking about outside acts
steps.stepSummary: Someone who sprinkles inside and plans to burn the fats and pour the leftover blood outside tomorrow has also not made פיגול, because the thought is inside but the acts are outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stood inside and said, 'I am sprinkling in order to burn the sacrificial parts and pour out the leftover blood tomorrow,' it is not פיגול, because it is a thought inside about an act done outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposite example. This time the thought is made inside, about acts that happen outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning the אימורים and pouring the leftover blood are done outside, at the outer מזבח. Step 15 said a thought about outside acts can make פיגול. But that only works if the thought is also made outside. When the place of the thought and the place of the act do not match, it is never פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: sprinkling (the blood)
the fats and parts of the offering burned on the מזבח
the leftover blood, poured at the base of the מזבח
with the intention of, in order to

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, a פיגול thought counts only when the thought and the act it is about are in the same area: both outside.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 15 said 'about something done outside, it is פיגול.' This example shows that is not enough by itself. The thought must also be made outside.

phrases.english: If he was standing inside and said:
"I am sprinkling in order
to burn the sacrificial parts
and to pour out the leftover blood tomorrow" —
he did not make it piggul,
because it is a thought inside
about something done outside.
phrases.notes: The words 'does not make piggul' are left out here, but they are understood from the first example.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror-image example to step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thought inside about an act done outside also does not make פיגול.

steps.title: Outside thought about an outside act does make פיגול
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן stands outside and slaughters with the plan to pour the leftover blood or burn the fats tomorrow, the offering is פיגול, because both the thought and the planned act are outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he was standing outside and said, 'I am slaughtering so that I can pour out the leftover blood tomorrow,' or 'so that I can burn the fats tomorrow,' he has made it פיגול. This is because it is an outside thought about something that is done outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list of cases. Now it gives the case where פיגול does work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases (Steps 16-17), one part was inside and one part was outside, so there was no פיגול. Here the slaughtering is outside, and the planned acts are also outside: the leftover blood is poured at the outside altar and the fats are burned there. When everything matches on the outside, the wrong-time thought makes the offering פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: He made the offering פיגול, so it can no longer be used, because he planned to do a service at the wrong time
The leftover blood that is poured out after the sprinkling
The fats and parts of the animal that are burned on the altar
To burn on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול only happens when the thought and the act are both outside. If one is inside and the other is outside, there is no פיגול.

phrases.english: But if he was standing outside,
and said: 'I am slaughtering'
'in order to pour out the leftover blood tomorrow,'
phrases.notes: Pouring the leftover blood is done at the outside altar, so this is an outside act.

phrases.english: or 'to burn the fats tomorrow' –
he has made it פיגול,
because it is a thought outside
about something that is done outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the positive case that stands against the two negative cases in Steps 16-17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering outside with a plan to do an outside service (pouring leftover blood or burning fats) at the wrong time makes the offering פיגול.

steps.title: What is the source? A פסוק that seems to teach nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks for the source and brings the פסוק comparing the פר כהן משיח to the שלמים. He then asks what this comparison could possibly teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What is the פסוק? 'As it is taken off from the ox of the peace offering.' But what, then, do we learn from the ox of the peace offering?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי looks for the פסוק behind רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule. He quotes it and points out a problem: the comparison seems pointless. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the fats of the פר כהן משיח are removed like the fats of the שלמים. But the section about this bull already lists all of those fats itself, so the comparison seems to teach nothing new. Because it looks pointless for that, it must be there to teach something else, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק? (What is the source?)
Just as it is removed (taken off)
The ox of the peace offering
But what did we learn? (a question showing the פסוק seems to teach nothing)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
What is the verse?
'As it is taken off'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:10, about the bull brought by the כהן משיח.

phrases.english: 'from the ox of the peace offering' –
but what did we learn
from the ox of the peace offering, then?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind the rule, and why the פסוק compares the פר כהן משיח to the שלמים when the comparison seems to teach nothing.

steps.title: The פסוק compares the פר כהן משיח to the שלמים for פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The comparison teaches that just as the שלמים only become פיגול through thoughts and acts on the outside altar, so too the פר כהן משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק compares the bull of the כהן משיח to the ox of the peace offering. The ox of the peace offering only becomes פיגול when its acts and thoughts are about the outside altar. So too, the bull of the כהן משיח only becomes פיגול when its thoughts and acts are about the outside altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers his own question. The comparison is a הקש, and it teaches the rule of פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything about the שלמים happens at the outside altar, so its פיגול can only involve the outside altar. The פסוק links the פר כהן משיח to the שלמים, so it too only becomes פיגול when the thought and the act both involve the outside altar. That is exactly why the inside-outside mixes in Steps 16-17 do not make פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares (makes a הקש, which links two subjects so they share the same laws)
The bull brought by the anointed כהן גדול for a sin done by mistake
The outside altar, in the courtyard
Its thoughts and its acts

steps.whyThisMatters: This הקש is the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי's whole rule: inside thoughts and inside acts cannot create פיגול.

phrases.english: Rather, it compares the bull of the anointed priest
to the ox of the peace offering;
just as the ox of the peace offering –
only when its acts and thoughts are
phrases.notes: The word פיגול is not written, but that is the topic: it only becomes פיגול this way.

phrases.english: about the outside altar,
so too the bull of the anointed priest –
only when its thoughts and acts are
about the outside altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַקִּישׁ פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ לְשׁוֹר זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19 by explaining the comparison as a הקש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק makes a הקש: like the שלמים, the פר כהן משיח only becomes פיגול through thoughts and acts that involve the outside altar.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר, who taught in the name of רבי יוסי that only outside thoughts about outside acts make פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר, who said this in the name of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic by giving the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's teaching in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי (Step 15) is now accepted as the הלכה. So in practice, an inside thought or an inside act cannot create פיגול in these offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows (this opinion)
In the name of

steps.confusionAlert: The 'רבי יוסי' here is רבי יוסי הגלילי from Step 15, not the more famous רבי יוסי (בן חלפתא).
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: פיגול in these offerings needs both the thought and the act to involve the outside altar.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Elazar
who said it in the name of Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: This goes back to Step 15, where רבי אלעזר quoted רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on the ברייתא whose source was just explained.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי: פיגול only happens when the thought and the act both involve the outside altar.

steps.title: רבא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new statement by רבא. The content of his statement follows in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by introducing a new speaker, רבא. This line is only the opening, so his actual point comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have just finished the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר: only outside thoughts about outside acts make פיגול. Now a new אמורא, רבא, is about to add his own statement. Nothing has been said yet in this line. It only tells us who is speaking next.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to find a ruling in this line by itself. It is only the introduction, and רבא's actual statement comes next.

phrases.english: Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב's final ruling in step 21, the גמרא brings in a new statement from רבא. This line only introduces the speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This line only names the speaker. רבא's ruling or point appears in the text that follows.
